text: The Wyrmwood Reserve has reintroduced pine martens, with 12 animals released into the woodland on Tuesday as part of a conservation project led by the Cereden Wildlife Trust and the local forestry board. The release, carried out at dawn near the reserve’s northern boundary, follows months of habitat preparation and monitoring. Rangers said the nocturnal predators are expected to help control grey squirrel numbers and strengthen the area’s woodland ecosystem. “This is a major step in restoring balance to Wyrmwood,” said reserve manager Elin Voss. The animals were fitted with temporary tracking collars, and field teams will monitor their movements over the next six months.
